headline.text: Kymenlaakso lags national levels in crude curative treatment at 19.3% (95% CI 16.3–22.7) versus 27.0% and crude MDT recording at 0.5% (95% CI 0.2–1.5) versus 6.0%.

details.text: The county's crude curative treatment share, which is not adjusted for age or stage, is 19.3% (95% CI 16.3–22.7; n=114/591) alongside the national 27.0% (4009/14873), and the 95% confidence interval excludes the national value.

In figures digitised from Kuva 16 with precision ±0.5 percentage points, the age-adjusted curative share gap holds for men at 17.9% (95% CI 13.9–22.9) versus 26.7% nationally, as the 95% confidence interval excludes the dashed national reference line, whereas for women at 22.6% (95% CI 16.8–29.3) versus 26.9% nationally, the 95% confidence interval includes it.

Across overlapping treatment categories that are not mutually exclusive, Kymenlaakso's crude shares exceed national values for life-prolonging treatment at 37.6% (95% CI 33.8–41.5; n=222/591) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) and symptomatic treatment at 51.3% (95% CI 47.2–55.3; n=303/591) versus 39.5% (5871/14873), with each 95% confidence interval excluding the national value.

Crude MDT meeting recording is 0.5% (95% CI 0.2–1.5; n=3/591) compared with 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, though HILMO captures specialist procedures only from direct patient contacts so this measures recording practice rather than care.

headline.text: A crude 16.4% (95% CI 13.7–19.6) share with no treatment record versus 27.5% nationally suggests Kymenlaakso's curative gap is not only a recording artefact, though stage is unmeasured.

details.text: Kymenlaakso's crude share with no treatment record within 12 months—mixing patients who had no treatment and unrecorded treatment—is 16.4% (95% CI 13.7–19.6; n=97/591) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally (95% CI excludes the national value); read as a data-quality signal, this inference is consistent with relatively complete treatment recording, making a recording artefact less likely.

However, this signal is not direct evidence of complete treatment capture—a journal article finding that HILMO matches the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types concerns diagnosis concordance only—and missing stage at diagnosis for a large share of patients nationally prevents stage adjustment.

Public data also leave early pathway stages unseen: symptom onset is unmeasured, outpatient primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is unmentioned, imaging appears only indirectly as the basis of diagnosis in approximately 20% of cases, and referral, specialist visit, and treatment start dates are absent.

Preliminary, unpublished national figures average 155 days from symptoms to treatment in Finland versus 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark—with 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care, the longest stage—while the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion.

headline.text: The team recommends reporting lung cancer access times using THL 21/2016 definitions, adopting standardised referrals and diagnostic coordination, and publishing county recording completeness for stage, drugs, and MDT.

details.text: The team recommends reporting lung cancer access times across referral, specialist visit, diagnosis, and treatment start using THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions and flagging stalled handovers, as Finland currently lacks unified national access monitoring while the roadmap plans cancer-specific access times in 2026–2028 and the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation is due before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

The team recommends adopting a standard referral template and a persistent-symptoms referral rule after a normal X-ray—as set out in KYS's regional pathway document—plus a named diagnostic-phase contact person, since mentor insight notes weak referrals receive lower specialist urgency and the roadmap plans standardised referral criteria and care-coordinator guidance in 2026–2028 for county adoption in 2029–2031.

Given Kymenlaakso's 0.5% (95% CI 0.2–1.5; n=3/591) crude MDT recording share versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally and incomplete national lung cancer data storage, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding while the roadmap plans a national quality registry targeting 90% data coverage including stage alongside uniform recording instructions.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
rec:3.location: §3. Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding
